title: Beyond Attack Success Rate: Cost-Aware Metric for Evaluating Iterative LLM Jailbreaks
abstract: arXiv:2610.26589v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Attack success rate (ASR) evaluates jailbreaks against large language models without accounting for repeated calls to the victim model. Yet each additional call gives the deployed system another opportunity to detect the attack and intervene. We introduce $\mathrm{ASR}_{\mathrm{STEP}}$, which penalizes additional victim-model calls while retaining binary success judgments. Our evaluation considers GCG, PAIR with a step budget, and a single-step PAP baseline on JailBreakBench across three model families. GCG's scores decrease by 7.0-8.7 percentage points after discounting, while PAP's remain unchanged. While for PAIR attack, we see a wider discounting range between 3.4-12 percentage points, showing that the "step" quantity differs per iterative strategy. Reporting both metrics makes the discount due to repeated victim-model interaction explicit. Code is available here: https://github.com/SuELS-Group/beyond_asr.

translated_title: 超越攻击成功率：用于评估迭代式大语言模型越狱攻击的成本感知指标
translated_abstract: 攻击成功率（ASR）在评估针对大语言模型的越狱攻击时，未考虑对受害模型的重复调用。然而，每一次额外的调用都为已部署系统提供了另一次检测攻击并进行干预的机会。我们提出了 ASR_STEP，它在保留二元成功判断的同时，对额外的受害模型调用进行惩罚。我们的评估在 JailBreakBench 上考察了 GCG、带有步数预算的 PAIR，以及单步的 PAP 基线方法，涵盖三个模型系列。经过折扣后，GCG 的分数下降了 7.0-8.7 个百分点，而 PAP 的分数保持不变。对于 PAIR 攻击，我们观察到更宽的折扣范围，介于 3.4-12 个百分点之间，这表明“步数”这一数量因迭代策略而异。同时报告这两种指标可以明确揭示因重复与受害模型交互而产生的折扣。代码已发布于：https://github.com/SuELS-Group/beyond_asr。
tldr: 提出成本感知评估指标 ASR_STEP，通过对重复调用受害模型的次数进行惩罚，弥补了传统攻击成功率指标在评估迭代式越狱攻击时忽视调用成本的缺陷。
en_tdlr: We propose ASR_STEP, a cost-aware evaluation metric that penalizes repeated victim-model calls, addressing the limitation of attack success rate in evaluating iterative LLM jailbreaks.
